scheme_name: Scheme for Campaign, Seminar and Sports under Disability Sector
description:
The Scheme for Campaign, Seminar and Sports under the Disability Sector was launched by the Government of India in the year 2018. 

This scheme aims to promote awareness and understanding of disability issues among the general public. 

The initiative is part of the broader efforts by the Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment. 

The ministry focuses on the welfare of persons with disabilities in India. 

The objectives of this scheme include organizing campaigns to raise awareness about the rights and capabilities of persons with disabilities. 

It also aims to facilitate seminars that provide a platform for discussion on disability-related topics. 

The scheme encourages the organization of sports events for persons with disabilities to promote inclusivity and participation. 

The specific measurable targets of the scheme include conducting at least 100 awareness campaigns annually. 

Additionally, the scheme aims to organize a minimum of 50 seminars each year. 

The sports events under this scheme target participation from at least 5,000 persons with disabilities annually. 

The benefits of this scheme are multifaceted. 

Participants in the campaigns and seminars receive educational materials and resources. 

These resources aim to enhance their understanding of disability rights and available government schemes. 

The sports events provide opportunities for physical activity and competition. 

This promotes not only health but also social interaction among participants. 

Financial assistance is provided to organizing bodies for conducting these events. 

The amount allocated for each campaign or seminar can go up to INR 5 lakhs. 

For sports events, the financial support can reach up to INR 10 lakhs. 

Eligibility for this scheme is defined clearly. 

Organizations that are registered under the Societies Registration Act of 1860 or similar acts can apply. 

These organizations must have a proven track record of working with persons with disabilities. 

There are no specific age limits for participants in the campaigns and seminars. 

However, for sports events, participants must be persons with disabilities aged between 8 and 40 years. 

Income criteria are not explicitly defined for organizations. 

However, they must demonstrate financial stability and capability to manage the funds. 

The application process for this scheme involves several steps. 

Interested organizations must submit a detailed project proposal to the Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment. 

The proposal should outline the objectives, target audience, and expected outcomes of the campaign or seminar. 

Organizations must include a budget breakdown for the proposed activities. 

Required documents include the registration certificate of the organization. 

Additionally, organizations must provide proof of past activities related to disability. 

Once the proposal is submitted, it undergoes a review process by the ministry. 

Successful applicants receive a sanction order detailing the amount of financial assistance. 

The timeline for the application process typically spans three months from the submission date. 

Organizations are encouraged to apply at least six months before the planned event. 

Disbursement of funds occurs in two installments. 

The first installment is released upon approval of the proposal. 

The second installment is released after submission of utilization certificates and reports. 

The implementing authority for this scheme is the Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment. 

The Department of Empowerment of Persons with Disabilities oversees the execution of the scheme. 

Contact details for the ministry can be found on their official website. 

The ministry provides a helpline for queries related to the scheme. 

This helpline can be reached at 1800-11-2001. 

The scheme also aligns with the Rights of Persons with Disabilities Act 2016. 

This act emphasizes the need for awareness and empowerment of persons with disabilities. 

Statistics indicate that approximately 2.68 crore people in India are registered as persons with disabilities. 

This highlights the importance of initiatives like this scheme. 

The scheme also aims to foster collaboration with NGOs and civil society organizations. 

This collaboration is crucial for reaching a wider audience. 

The sports events organized under this scheme include various disciplines. 

These disciplines cater to different types of disabilities. 

The events are designed to encourage participation at local, state, and national levels. 

The scheme also promotes the celebration of International Day of Persons with Disabilities. 

This day is observed on December 3rd each year. 

The ministry encourages organizations to plan events around this date. 

The scheme has seen participation from various states across India. 

States like Maharashtra, Tamil Nadu, and Uttar Pradesh have actively engaged in organizing events. 

Reports indicate that over 10,000 individuals have benefited from the sports events in the last year alone. 

The scheme has received positive feedback from participants and organizations alike. 

Many organizations have reported increased awareness and understanding of disability issues. 

The sports events have also led to the discovery of talented athletes among persons with disabilities. 

These athletes have gone on to represent India in national and international competitions. 

The scheme is part of a larger framework of welfare initiatives for persons with disabilities. 

It complements other schemes such as the Assistance to Disabled Persons for Purchase/Fitting of Aids and Appliances. 

Overall, the Scheme for Campaign, Seminar and Sports under the Disability Sector plays a crucial role. 

It enhances the visibility of disability issues in India. 

It also promotes the inclusion of persons with disabilities in various aspects of society. 

The scheme continues to evolve based on feedback and changing needs. 

It remains committed to fostering a more inclusive society for all individuals. 

The government encourages continuous participation from stakeholders in the disability sector. 

This ensures that the scheme remains relevant and effective in achieving its objectives.
